subject: Logic 13 control bar: what the Play checkbox and the Stop button do while playing, and what each display mode shows
question: Which control bar action stops playback on Logic 13 through Accessibility, and what does each display mode show?

reverify.command: With Logic 13 running a disposable project copy and the control bar display on Beats & Project, play from bar 12, then AXPress the AXCheckBox with identifier controlBar/playButton and sample the playhead and its AXValue for 5 s; after it, AXPress the AXButton with identifier controlBar/stopButton and sample again. Then switch the display popup through the display modes and read the playhead position group and the tempo slider.
reverify.expected: Pressing the Play checkbox while playing leaves AXValue at 1 and the playhead jumps back to bar 12 and keeps moving; pressing the Stop button turns Play to 0 and the playhead holds. In Beats the playhead reads bar.beat.division.tick and the tempo slider is absent.
reverify.cost: About two minutes against a disposable project copy; closes only that copy.

method: Server drove Logic over stdio (debug build, one channel at a time through LOGIC_MCP_DEBUG_ONLY_CHANNEL=Accessibility for the Accessibility route); a separate AX probe read the control bar controls and the Playhead Position group at 0.4 to 0.6 s intervals as the independent reading. Each run used a fresh ditto copy of a disposable fixture, closed without saving afterwards. Nothing was clicked by coordinates.

observations.what: AXPress on the Play checkbox while playing
observations.result: playback restarted from the start position and continued

observations.what: AXPress on the Stop button while playing
AXPress on the Stop button while stopped
observations.result: Go to Beginning: the playhead moved from bar 15 to bar 1

observations.what: product transport.stop through the Accessibility route before the change, three runs
observations.answer: State C readback_mismatch, button Play, action axpress, fallback_unsafe true

observations.what: product transport.stop through the Accessibility route after the change, three runs
observations.answer: State A, button Stop, action axpress, verify_source ax_transport_state

observations.what: product transport.stop through the default route (CGEvent keypad 0) before the change, three runs
display modes, idle playhead and tempo slider

modes.Beats & Project (large): bar, beat, division, tick; tempo slider 120
modes.Beats & Time: bar, beat; time (hour, minute, second); no tempo slider
modes.Beats & Time (large): bar, beat, division, tick; time to subframe; no tempo slider
modes.Beats: bar, beat, division, tick; no tempo slider
modes.Time: time to subframe only; no bar position; no tempo slider
modes.Custom: bar, beat, division, tick; time to subframe; further position groups; no tempo slider

observations.what: playhead in Beats while playing, three readings

conclusion: On the measured host the Play checkbox is not a stop: pressed while playing it restarts playback from the start position and stays on. The AXButton controlBar/stopButton stops playback when pressed while playing and is Go to Beginning when pressed while stopped, so it is pressed only while Play reads on and confirmed by Play reading off. In the Beats display the tempo slider is absent; pause there is not supported and refuses before any write.
limits: One Logic 13.0 build 7801 host, ko-KR, one fixture. Other Logic versions and locales were not measured; the identifier controlBar/stopButton is not localized but its presence on Logic 12 is unmeasured, so a bar without it keeps the older Play-checkbox path.

The Accessibility route was isolated with a debug-only channel restriction; the reporter's route to it (why the CGEvent rung did not act on their host) was not measured. On this host the default route stopped playback before the change in three of three runs.
A paused transport's Stop button description was not recorded separately from the playing one beyond the pause run, where it read the same as while playing.
Pause and play from a paused start were not driven in any display mode for this record; with the tempo unreadable they refuse before any write.

canon_not_applicable.reason: This record measures runtime Accessibility roles, identifiers and transport behavior. It adds no Apple label vocabulary and claims no string-corpus value.
